name: E2 dehydrohalogenation (Zaitsev)
outcome: Typically 60-90%; more substituted alkene usually predominates.
notes: A small strong base usually favors the more substituted Zaitsev alkene.

name: E2 elimination of alkyl chloride
outcome: Typically 50-85%; antiperiplanar elimination gives an alkene.
notes: Requires an antiperiplanar beta hydrogen and leaving group.

name: E2 dehydrohalogenation (Hofmann)
outcome: Typically 50-85%; less substituted alkene is favored.
notes: A bulky base preferentially removes the least hindered beta hydrogen.

name: Acid-catalysed alcohol dehydration
outcome: Typically 50-90%; Zaitsev alkene with rearrangement risk.
notes: Secondary and tertiary alcohols dehydrate readily; carbocation rearrangements can occur.

name: E2 elimination of alkyl iodide
outcome: Typically 65-95%; more substituted alkene usually predominates.
notes: Iodide is an excellent leaving group; stereochemistry follows the required antiperiplanar arrangement.

name: E2 elimination of alkyl tosylate
outcome: Typically 55-90%; alkene regioselectivity follows base size and conformation.
notes: Sulfonate esters are strong leaving groups; substrate conformation controls antiperiplanar access.

name: E2 elimination of alkyl mesylate
conditions: CH2Cl2 or THF, rt to reflux
notes: A non-nucleophilic base favors elimination over substitution while preserving E2 stereospecificity.

name: E1 elimination of tertiary alkyl halide
outcome: Typically 40-80%; Zaitsev alkene mixture with rearrangement possible.
notes: Ionization forms a carbocation, so substitution competes and stereospecificity is low.

name: POCl3-pyridine alcohol dehydration
notes: A phosphorylated leaving group undergoes base-promoted E2 elimination under nonaqueous conditions.

name: Hofmann elimination
outcome: Typically 40-80%; least substituted alkene usually predominates.
notes: Steric and leaving-group effects favor removal of the most accessible beta hydrogen.

name: Cope elimination of amine oxide
outcome: Typically 50-90%; syn alkene elimination through a five-membered transition state.
notes: The intramolecular syn elimination proceeds without added base and is strongly conformation-dependent.

name: Zinc dehalogenation of vicinal dibromide
outcome: Typically 60-95%; alkene formed by reductive dehalogenation.
notes: Stereochemical outcome depends on substrate geometry and the surface-mediated elimination pathway.
